    Where the numbers come from

    Everything here is published data; nothing is simulated.

    • Your home: the county parcel file you supplied (Henrico and Hanover records for ZIP 23059), with Henrico sales recorded through Sept 30, 2026 added from Henrico County's parcel and assessment service (retrieved Oct 6, 2026): 2026 assessed value, prior-year assessed value, and last recorded sale price and date.
    • Neighborhood: FHFA All-Transactions House Price Index for your home's county, Henrico or Hanover, annual through 2025. The ZIP-level median in the strip above comes from the parcel file itself.
    • Virginia: FHFA All-Transactions HPI for Virginia, quarterly through Q2 2026.
    • United States: FHFA All-Transactions HPI for the U.S., quarterly through Q2 2026.

    Comparable sales come from the same parcel file: each home's most recent recorded sale. Sales that cover several parcels on one deed, look like non-market transfers, or were recorded before the home was built are left out. Under Close matching, homes in your own subdivision are allowed a wider size and age difference, since their location already matches.

    The estimated range adjusts each comp's price to your home. The adjustment rates were measured from about 1,600 sales in 23059 over the last three years (by home type, comparing homes within the same subdivision): size, bathrooms, bedrooms, age, market movement since the sale, and location between subdivisions with at least five sales. A rate is only used where the data shows a clear effect. The estimate is the median adjusted price. The range width comes from testing: the method was run on every market sale in 23059 over the past year, using only sales recorded before it, and the range is set wide enough to contain 8 in 10 of those results (about 3 in 4 when checked on sales held out of the calibration). Typical miss: 3–7% depending on home type.

    Index data from FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, checked Oct 6, 2026 (Q2 2026 is the latest FHFA release). Source: FHFA House Price Index®.

    How to read it

    The FHFA indexes track repeat sales and appraisals of the same single-family homes, so they measure price change rather than a typical price. The estimated line for your home applies that change to one of your home's real values, the same approach as FHFA's own house price calculator. It can't see renovations, additions or anything specific to your street.

    Annual county values are plotted at mid-year and quarterly values at mid-quarter. The most recent county figure (2025) is aligned with the January 1, 2026 assessment. Sales far from what the index implies are flagged, since they are often family transfers or new-construction lot sales rather than market prices.
